explanation: Aluminium oxide, an amphoteric oxide, reacts with hydrochloric acid like a base would, forming aluminium chloride and water.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A white, insoluble aluminium oxide powder sitting in a colourless dilute hydrochloric acid solution.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A colourless aluminium chloride solution; the white powder has dissolved away.
beaker_view.observation: The white aluminium oxide powder gradually dissolves into the acid, leaving a clear, colourless solution behind with no bubbling or precipitate.
